statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 5 (low) through every remaining scheduled CME weekend halt hour and 9 to 13 (low) across the six reopen and Asian-session hours; Stress 26 (moderate) now, building to a 47 (elevated) peak at the reopen; Confidence 58 (medium-low).
recommendation: Descriptive only. CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and is scheduled to reopen at Sunday 30 August 22:00 UTC, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in the first eighteen hours covered here and Tail stays far below the block threshold for both NQ_FUTURES and NAS100_CFD. Stress runs from 26 to 47 as unpriced weekend information accumulates ahead of the reopen and the 1 to 4 September data stack, and Confidence eases from 58 to 47 as the Friday reference tape ages before recovering to 67 once live price discovery would resume. No danger window is published, because no observed one-way structure exists and none can form while the venue is closed.
headline: Weekend halt, hour 32: NDX 29,433.43 (-0.70%) closed near the low of a 29,383.92 to 29,752.78 range, NQ 29,491.75, VIX 14.43, with September hike odds near 57% after Jackson Hole; Globex reopens Sunday 22:00 UTC as the nineteenth slot of this window
body: CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and is scheduled to reopen at Sunday 30 August 22:00 UTC, which falls inside this window as its final six slots, so the first eighteen hours assessed here cover a closed venue with no Nasdaq-100 price discovery; NQ last traded at 20:59 UTC on 28 August. The reference tape was re-verified against primary sources this run and was unchanged: cash NDX closed 29,433.43, down 0.70 percent or 208.13 points, inside a 29,383.92 to 29,752.78 range against a 29,641.56 previous close, finishing near the lower end of that range; NQ futures last printed 29,491.75, down 0.69 percent or 204.00 points, in a 29,436.75 to 29,811.50 range; VIX finished at 14.43, down 0.55 percent, within a 14.13 to 14.84 range against a 14.51 previous close. The Federal Reserve H.15 daily release still carries 27 August as its most recent column, at 4.20 percent for the 2-year and 4.67 percent for the 10-year, so Friday's own move is known only through market reporting: the 10-year closed near 4.72 percent, up about four basis points, and the policy-sensitive 2-year rose roughly twelve basis points to about 4.36 percent after Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks lifted the priced odds of a September increase to about 57 percent from roughly 35 percent the prior day. Crude closed slightly lower, WTI at 83.44 and Brent at 88.29, which does not corroborate a supply-driven shock despite the unresolved Strait of Hormuz disruption, where transit volumes remain far below normal; the Iran-Oman framework for a temporary corridor and joint mine clearing, published on 25 and 26 August, is a de-escalation vector that remains unimplemented while permanent-route talks are described as taking 30 to 60 days. Friday's session internals were split, with semiconductors broadly lower against firmer large-cap software and consumer names, a configuration that reduces directional conviction rather than establishing the persistent one-way structure Tail is defined against; the shared delayed cross-asset context file was stale at this assessment time and carried no usable futures section, so it served only as latest-session corroboration of that split and this run rests on independent verification from primary sources. Tail is therefore held at 5 for every remaining halt hour and published conditionally between 9 and 13 across the reopen and Asian-session slots; Stress builds from 26 to a 47 peak at the reopen as unpriced information accumulates ahead of a dense 1 to 4 September calendar that includes ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS, ADP and the Beige Book, Broadcom's fiscal Q3 results, ISM Services and the August employment report; Confidence decays to 47 on tape age before recovering to 67 once an open market could again be observed.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours run from 04:00 UTC on Saturday 29 August to 03:00 UTC on Sunday 30 August, hours 8 to 31 of the CME weekend halt. The mode was normal in every slot and the mapped policy state never left EA_ON. Tail held the 5 floor in all twenty-four hours, because no venue was open to produce the price-path evidence Tail is defined against. Stress rose from 23 through 24 to a 25 plateau that held for the final twenty-two slots, while Confidence declined steadily from 81 to 59 as the Friday reference tape aged without any new observation to refresh it. No slot was unavailable and no assessment in the window was revised with later information.
outlookSummary: The first eighteen hours of this window fall inside the CME weekend halt, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in them; Tail is held at 5 throughout, keeping the mapped policy state at EA_ON, and the dominant mode is normal in those slots because a closed market has no structure to classify rather than because conditions are assessed as calm. Stress climbs from 26 to 43 across those hours as unpriced weekend information accumulates against Friday's hawkish front-end repricing and the dense 1 to 4 September macro week, while Confidence decays from 58 to 47 purely through the ageing of the reference tape. The final six slots are the scheduled Globex reopen at 22:00 UTC, the first full hour after it, the hour around the Tokyo cash open and the established Asian session into the European handover: they are the first hours in this window that can host observable structure and are published with conditional Tail readings of 13, 12, 11, 10, 10 and 9, each of which keeps the mapped state at EA_ON. Stress peaks at 47 in the reopen hour, where thin-book whipsaw rather than a sustained one-way trend is the expected failure mode, and then eases as the backlog clears into an open market, while Confidence recovers to 67. Those reopen readings are conditional scenarios; no post-reopen price path has been observed at this assessment time, and the actual structure will be scored in later runs.

forecast.analysis: Halt hour 41. Stress 33. Roughly nine hours remain to the scheduled 22:00 UTC Globex reopen, and each further hour of accumulation enlarges the gap the market must price at once. That is a Stress mechanism; Tail would respond only if the ensuing path denied retracement.

forecast.analysis: First full hour after the scheduled reopen. If the opening print is absorbed with two-way trade and visible retracement, Tail eases to 12 and Confidence recovers to 61 as live observation returns. A gap that extends without pullback would instead be the first genuine Tail evidence of the week.

Confidence recovers because live observation returns, not because risk fell

forecast.analysis: Tokyo cash open. Asian participation normally deepens the book and improves the retracement record, so Tail is published at 11. The checkpoint to watch is whether the reopen gap is defended or faded once a second regional session is involved in price discovery.

forecast.analysis: Established Asian session. Tail 10 assumes orderly price discovery with observable pullbacks. The invalidation is explicit: repeated extension after failed retracements, or NQ holding near a session extreme, would justify a higher reading than the one published here.

forecast.analysis: Mid-Asian session. Scores are held rather than extrapolated further, because projecting continued decay this far past the reopen without any observation would overstate what is known. Stress eases to 40 as the weekend backlog is progressively absorbed by an open market.
